desc: Prove per-element cost c(x)=number of base-4 digits, and derive per-query formula answer = max(c(r), ceil(total_cost(l..r)/2)); verified on [[1,2],[2,4]]->3 and [[2,6]]->4.
Implement `minOperations` with prefix-cost P(n) over powers of 4, looping queries computing max(c(r), ceil((P(r)-P(l-1))/2)) and summing.
Confirm closed-form prefix P(n)=pref[L-1]+L*(n-4^(L-1)+1) handles exact powers of 4 (bisect_right), l=1 (P(0)=0), and r up to 1e9 (max cost 15, arrays sized to 16).
Complexity sanity-check: O(log_4 r)~16 per query via bisect, O(Q*16) total, no per-range iteration; Python big ints handle sums up to ~7.5e14.
